blockMcqs.question: What defines a deadlock in a database?
options: A query that takes too long to execute
Two transactions each waiting on a lock the other holds
A transaction that acquires too many locks
A corrupted index preventing reads
blockMcqs.explanation: A deadlock is a circular wait where each transaction holds a lock needed by another, so none can proceed.

blockMcqs.question: Which Coffman condition means a lock can't be taken away?
options: Hold and wait
Mutual exclusion
No preemption
Circular wait
blockMcqs.explanation: No preemption means locks are released only voluntarily; they cannot be forcibly taken from a holder.

blockMcqs.question: In a wait-for graph, what signals a deadlock?
options: A node with no outgoing edges
A cycle in the graph
More than two nodes
An edge pointing to itself
blockMcqs.explanation: A cycle means each transaction in the cycle waits on the next, and none can ever proceed — that is the definition of deadlock.

blockMcqs.question: What does the DBMS do after detecting a deadlock cycle?
options: Retries all transactions from the start
Aborts a chosen victim transaction
Adds more locks to break the cycle
Pauses all transactions indefinitely
blockMcqs.explanation: The DBMS picks a victim from the cycle and aborts it, releasing its locks so the remaining transactions can proceed.

blockMcqs.question: In wait-die, what happens when a younger transaction requests a lock held by an older one?
options: The younger waits indefinitely
The older is aborted
The younger dies (aborts)
Both transactions are aborted
blockMcqs.explanation: In wait-die, a younger transaction requesting an older transaction's lock is aborted (dies). Only older-requests-younger allows waiting.

blockMcqs.question: Why does wait-die prevent deadlocks?
options: It allows any transaction to steal locks
Younger transactions never wait on older ones
All transactions request locks at startup
It detects cycles before granting locks
blockMcqs.explanation: In wait-die, a younger transaction is aborted rather than made to wait on an older one, so no cycle of waits can form.

blockMcqs.question: What is the main drawback of using timeouts to handle deadlocks?
options: Timeouts require a wait-for graph
They only work with two transactions
Slow-but-valid transactions may be aborted unnecessarily
They prevent all concurrency
blockMcqs.explanation: A timeout can't distinguish a deadlocked transaction from one that is legitimately slow, so it may abort healthy work.

blockMcqs.question: Which criterion is most commonly used to select a deadlock victim?
options: The transaction with the most committed rows
The oldest transaction in the system
The transaction with the least work done
The transaction holding the most shared locks
blockMcqs.explanation: Aborting the least-progressed transaction minimises rollback cost, making it the cheapest choice for victim.
